We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied 29646 to target, got product(s) (three possible). The first product seems to be a protected version with Si group. The apply_template result gave three tuples: each is a possible precursor set? Actually apply_template returns list of precursor SMILES strings (maybe each is a tuple of precursors). The result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO',))"

So three possible precursors each single molecule? Actually each tuple contains one SMILES. So after first step, we have three possible intermediates.

We need to continue with template 1914389 applied to one of those intermediates. We checked matching for first one (with Si group attached to O). It matched True and applying gave two products: ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC').

So applying 1914389 to that intermediate yields two fragments: a larger fragment (still with Si) and a small fragment "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". That seems like a disconnection.

Now next template 1914390 should be applied to the product(s) from previous step? The order is fixed: after 1914389, we must apply 1914390 to the resulting molecules (maybe to the larger fragment). We attempted to check matching for "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC" with 1914390, got False. Also other candidates didn't match.

Maybe we need to choose a different branch: maybe apply 1914389 to a different intermediate from step1 that yields a different product that matches 1914390.

Let's examine other two precursors from step1: second: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". Third: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO". Let's test matching for 1914389 on those.
